title: Set the union wage

predict.q: The union raises the wage from the monopsony wage of £10 to £12. What happens to employment?

options.fb: That is the competitive-market result. Here, at £12, the firm no longer has to raise everyone's pay to add a worker, so it hires more.
At a flat £12 the cost of an extra worker is £12, not the rising MCL, so the firm hires up to the supply curve: 10 → 14.
The union wage changes the cost of an extra worker from the rising MCL to a flat £12, so the hiring decision changes.

task: Move the union wage slider to £12, then from £8 to £18, and watch employment.

target.do: Move the union wage slider from £10 to £12, then press Check.

takeaway: Between the monopsony wage and the MRP at the monopsony level of employment, a union wage can raise employment; push higher and jobs fall. At £12 the firm hires up to the supply curve: pay **and** employment rise, £10 → £12 and 10 → 14 workers.
